questions.q: Why does this lesson describe Managed Instance as much closer to on-prem SQL Server than Azure SQL Database, tying back to Lesson 3?
options: Because it trades a little PaaS convenience for near-complete SQL Server surface area, so most parity gaps from Lesson 73 disappear
Because Managed Instance runs on physical hardware the DBA manages directly
Because Managed Instance is actually identical in every respect to a SQL Server VM
Because Azure SQL Database and Managed Instance are the exact same product with different names
questions.explain: This lesson directly ties back to the Lesson 3 comparison: Managed Instance sits between Azure SQL Database and a full VM in feature parity.

questions.q: Which three capabilities does this lesson say migrate to Managed Instance largely unchanged?
options: Cross-database queries, native SQL Server Agent, and linked servers/CLR/Service Broker
Elastic Jobs, BACPAC import, and Database Migration Service
Azure Monitor alerts, Resource Governor, and Query Store
Dynamic data masking, row-level security, and TDE
questions.explain: These are exactly the capabilities that were parity gaps for Azure SQL Database in the previous lesson, but work natively here.

questions.q: What is the real native migration path into Managed Instance, per this lesson?
options: BACKUP DATABASE ... TO URL on-prem, followed by RESTORE DATABASE ... FROM URL on Managed Instance, using the same storage account URL
Exporting a BACPAC and importing it, exactly as with Azure SQL Database
There is no supported backup/restore path into Managed Instance
Manually copying .mdf files through Remote Desktop
questions.explain: Managed Instance supports native T-SQL restore straight from a blob storage URL — the one thing Azure SQL Database cannot do at all.

questions.q: What real gotchas does this lesson call out even though Managed Instance has higher feature parity?
options: Migration time for large restores, network requirements (VNet path to the instance and storage), and instance sizing done before cutover
Managed Instance cannot be reached from any network configuration
Migration to Managed Instance is always instantaneous regardless of database size
There are no real gotchas at all with Managed Instance migrations
questions.explain: Higher parity reduces feature-compatibility risk but doesn't eliminate the real operational friction of time, networking, and sizing.

questions.q: Why should instance sizing happen before cutover rather than reactively afterward, per this lesson?
options: Because the instance needs to already be sized for production load using the earlier sizing pass, not resized after go-live when performance problems are already affecting users
Because Azure automatically resizes instances in real time with zero cost
Because sizing has no effect on Managed Instance performance
Because instance sizing can only be changed once per year
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns against sizing reactively after go-live, tying back to the Lesson 71 sizing pass done during assessment.
